doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

chapter: Early drums, photos and the Laine home
title: Funerals only across the river
summary: Laine says he played all funerals from Algiers to Westwego, while Brookhoven and Braun held the contracts on the city side.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Let me just ask you one more question about funerals. You said you played with the... Did you ever play on this side of the river?
The funerals. Did you ever play on this side of the river?
Playing funerals? For funerals? No. Brookhoven and that fellow used to have that job. William J. Braun, Brookhoven.
They played on this side. You were on the other side then?
All my funerals, most of the funerals I played, that is all of them.

Was for, you say from, you would say from Algiers up into West Wigo. All the funerals over there. None on this side. Because they used to play all that funerals. It seemed, I don't know, they had some agreement, some contracts in there with these organizations. See, these men did, you understand? And of course, had to hire them in case of the funerals. Now, me, well, of course, I never had no contract with none of them and no agreements with none of them. And if they died, they wanted my band, they wanted us to ban. See?
